title: The matched-norm component test
takeaway: A concept's full representation is split into a small piece inside the J-space and a large remainder outside it, and the two pieces are injected at equal magnitude. Only the J-space piece moves the model's verbal reports: 59% swap success against 5% for the remainder, next to 88% for pure J-lens vectors. The paper takes this as evidence that the J-space is privileged for report, not merely correlated with it.
walkthrough:
The figure has three panels: a decomposition on the left, and one bar chart for each of the two report experiments from section 3.1.

The left panel shows the setup. A [[concept-vector]] is the model's full representation of one concept: the [[residual-stream]] activation recorded just before the Assistant responds to "Tell me about {concept}", with the mean over a baseline of 100 other concepts subtracted off. [[gradient-pursuit]], a greedy sparse-approximation algorithm, then finds the non-negative combination of the concept's top $k=16$ [[jacobian-lens]] vectors that best reconstructs the vector. That combination is the [[j-space-component]]; whatever it fails to capture is the non-J-space remainder. The split is lopsided. Across concepts and workspace layers, the J-space component carries a median of only 6-7% of the concept vector's variance. Roughly 93% of the representation lies outside the [[j-space]].

The middle panel repeats the [[think-of-a-category-task]] swap of Figure 6, with each component standing in for the pure J-lens vectors, and every perturbation rescaled to the same magnitude. The bars give the fraction of swap targets that reach the model's top-5 outputs, with [[wilson-interval]] error bars; dots mark the rate in each of the 14 categories. Pure J-lens vectors succeed on 88% of trials. The J-space component, despite holding a small fraction of the variance, succeeds on 59%. The non-J-space remainder, holding almost all of the variance, succeeds on 5%.

The right panel repeats the [[injected-thought-introspection]] experiment of Figure 7, injecting each component across the user turn and asking the model to report any implanted thought. Because injection effects depend on [[j-lens-steering]] strength, each bar shows the condition's best rate over a strength sweep, with that strength annotated. The section states the comparison qualitatively: the J-space component produces reports nearly as often as pure J-lens vectors, while the remainder produces few reports even at strengths several times larger. Exact right-panel rates appear only in the figure.

A follow-up control, described in the text rather than drawn here, closes the loop. The remainder's small effect might work by making later layers re-derive the concept inside the J-space. [[activation-clamping]] of the relevant lens coordinates to their clean-pass values blocks that route, and the remainder's effect falls to zero in the swap and nearly to zero in the injection.

terms.definition: The model's full representation of a concept: the residual-stream activation before the Assistant answers "Tell me about {concept}", mean-subtracted over a baseline of 100 other concepts.
The part of a concept vector that lies inside the J-space: the non-negative combination of its top k=16 J-lens vectors found by gradient pursuit.
What is left of the concept vector after the J-space component is removed; it carries roughly 93% of the vector's variance but lies outside the J-space.
Per-vocabulary-token directions identified by the Jacobian lens, each encoding the model's potential to verbalize that token. The concept vector is decomposed onto these.
The sparsity level of the decomposition: the number of J-lens vectors allowed into the J-space component of each concept vector.
The greedy sparse-approximation algorithm used to pick the 16 J-lens vectors and their non-negative weights that best reconstruct the concept vector.

The Figure 6 protocol: the model is told to think of an item from a category, and the intervention replaces its spontaneous choice with a target concept at matched magnitude, here along each component instead of pure J-lens vectors.

terms.term: fraction of swap targets reaching top-5
terms.definition: The middle panel's success metric: the share of trials in which the swapped-in target ends up among the model's five most likely outputs. Targets are drawn from outside the model's original top-10.
Wilson-score confidence intervals for the success proportions, drawn as error bars on each bar.
One dot per category (fourteen categories: languages, countries, animals, and so on) showing that category's own success rate around the pooled bar.
The Figure 7 protocol: the model is told a thought may have been implanted in its activations and is asked to report what it detects, while a vector is injected across the user turn.
The human side of the chat transcript. Injection happens on those token positions, and the model's report is read from the Assistant turn that follows.

A range of scaling factors applied to the injected vector. Each right-panel bar reports the best rate the condition achieves anywhere in the sweep, so no condition is penalized by a badly chosen strength.
The strength at which each condition peaked, printed next to its bar. The non-J-space remainder stays ineffective even at strengths several times larger than the others' best.
The set of activation-space points expressible as a sparse non-negative combination of J-lens vectors; the region the paper argues acts as the model's workspace.
The Claude model on which section 3.1's report experiments are illustrated; the figure caption itself does not restate the model.

numbers.meaning: The sparsity level k: how many J-lens vectors gradient pursuit may combine to form the J-space component of a concept vector.

Median share of a concept vector's variance carried by its J-space component, across concepts and workspace layers. The point of the figure is that this small piece does nearly all the causal work for report.
The complementary share of variance in the non-J-space remainder: almost the whole representation, yet nearly inert for verbal report at matched magnitude.
Swap success rate for pure J-lens vectors: the fraction of swap targets reaching the model's top-5 outputs. The ceiling the components are compared against.
Swap success rate when the swap runs along the concept vectors' J-space components. Approaches the 88% ceiling despite the component's small variance share.
Swap success rate for the non-J-space remainders at the same magnitude. Under the clamp control this residual effect falls to zero, so the paper attributes even it to leakage back into the J-space.
The success threshold in the swap experiment: a trial counts if the swapped-in target reaches the model's five most likely outputs.
The exclusion rule for choosing swap targets: only items not already in the model's ten most likely outputs are eligible, so success cannot come from concepts the model was about to say anyway.
The number of concept categories (a language, a country, an animal, and so on) in the think-of-a-category task; each contributes one dot per bar in the middle panel.
The confidence level of the Wilson intervals drawn as error bars on the success-rate bars.
The size of the baseline concept set whose mean activation is subtracted when extracting each concept vector.
How far the injection strength was pushed for the non-J-space remainder in the introspection experiment; even there it produces few reports, per the section text.

The remainder's effect under the clamp control (J-lens coordinates held at clean-pass values): exactly zero in the swap experiment, nearly zero in the injection experiment. Reported in the text, not drawn in the figure.
